weight. Suppose that every spanning tree in 𝐺 has even weight. Which of the
following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph 𝐺 ?

options.A: All edges in 𝐺 have even weight
options.B: All edges in 𝐺 have even weight OR all edges in 𝐺 have odd weight
options.C: In each cycle 𝐶 in 𝐺, all edges in 𝐶 have even weight
options.D:

have odd weight

questions.explaination: Let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$. For any chord $e \notin T$ creating a fundamental cycle $C$ with path $P \subseteq T$, $T' = T \setminus \{e'\} \cup \{e\}$ is also a spanning tree. Since $w(T)$ and $w(T')$ are both even, $w(e) \equiv w(e') \pmod 2$ for every edge on $C$. Thus all edges in cycle $C$ must have the same parity (either all even or all odd).

questions.question_text:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM,
average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.
A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming
average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal
places) to read the entire file from the disk is _________
questions.explaination: At 6000 RPM, one rotation takes $\frac{60}{6000} = 10\text{ ms}$. Average rotational latency $= 10/2 = 5\text{ ms}$. Transfer time per sector $= \frac{10\text{ ms}}{500} = 0.02\text{ ms}$. Time to access each random sector $= \text{seek} + \text{rotational latency} + \text{transfer} = 5 + 5 + 0.02 = 10.02\text{ ms}$. Total time for 3000 random sectors $= 3000 \times 10.02\text{ ms} = 30060\text{ ms} \approx 30.06$ seconds.

After receiving ACKs in the 1st RTT, slow start doubles $\text{cwnd}$ to $2\text{ MSS}$ during the 2nd RTT. Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of 108 bits/sec and a
maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal
in the medium is 2×108 meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required
for collision detection is _________
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging
questions.explaination: Propagation delay $T_p = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Velocity}} = \frac{500}{2 \times 10^8} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s} = 2.5\,\mu\text{s}$. For collision detection in CSMA/CD, transmission time must satisfy $T_t \ge 2 T_p = 5\,\mu\text{s}$. Minimum frame size $L = 2 T_p \times B = (5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}) \times 10^8\text{ bps} = 500$ bits.

questions.question_text:
A functional dependency 𝐹:⁡𝑋→𝑌 is termed as a useful functional dependency if
and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:
• 𝑋 is not the empty set.
• 𝑌 is not the empty set.
• Intersection of 𝑋 and 𝑌 is the empty set.

For a relation 𝑅 with 4 attributes, the total number of possible useful functional
dependencies is ________
questions.explaination: For each attribute $A$ among the 4 attributes, there are 3 mutually exclusive choices: $A \in X$, $A \in Y$, or $A \notin (X \cup Y)$, giving $3^4 = 81$ pairs of disjoint sets $(X, Y)$. We subtract cases where $X = \emptyset$ ($2^4 = 16$), where $Y = \emptyset$ ($2^4 = 16$), and add back the double-subtracted case where $X = Y = \emptyset$ ($1$). Total useful FDs $= 81 - 16 - 16 + 1 = 50$.

instruction format consists of an opcode field, an addressing mode field, two register
operand fields, and a 16-bit scalar field. If 8 addressing modes are to be supported,
the maximum number of unique opcodes possible for every addressing mode
is _________

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru
questions.explaination: Instruction length is 32 bits. Register fields: 16 registers need $\log_2 16 = 4$ bits each ($2 \times 4 = 8$ bits). Addressing mode: 8 modes need $\log_2 8 = 3$ bits. Scalar field: 16 bits. Remaining bits for opcode $= 32 - (3 + 8 + 16) = 5$ bits. The maximum number of unique opcodes possible for every addressing mode is $2^5 = 32$.

A non-pipelined instruction execution unit operating at 2 GHz takes an average of

operate on a 5-stage pipeline at 2 GHz. Assume that the ideal throughput of the
pipelined unit is 1 instruction per cycle. In the execution of program P,

questions.explaination: Average cycles per instruction in non-pipelined design: $\text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipe}} = 6$. In pipelined design: $\text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}} = 1 + (0.20 \times 2) + (0.20 \times 3) = 1 + 0.40 + 0.60 = 2.0$. Since clock frequency is 2 GHz in both, speedup $= \frac{\text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipe}}}{\text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}}} = \frac{6}{2.0} = 3.0$.

equally divided into two types, namely R-type and I-type, whose formats are shown
below.
R-type Instruction Format:
OPCODE UNUSED DST Register
SRC Register1
SRC Register 2
I-type Instruction Format:
OPCODE DST Register SRC Register # Immediate value/address
In the OPCODE, 1 bit is used to distinguish between I-type and R-type instructions
and the remaining bits indicate the operation. The processor has 50 architectural
registers, and all register fields in the instructions are of equal size.
Let 𝑋 be the number of bits used to encode the UNUSED field, 𝑌 be the number
of bits used to encode the OPCODE field, and 𝑍 be the number of bits used to
encode the immediate value/address field. The value of 𝑋+ 2𝑌+ 𝑍 is ________
questions.explaination: 150 distinct instructions split equally means 75 R-type and 75 I-type. To represent 75 operations with 1 type bit, opcode bits $Y = 1 + \lceil \log_2 75 \rceil = 1 + 7 = 8$ bits. 50 registers require $\lceil \log_2 50 \rceil = 6$ bits each. R-type has 3 register fields ($3 \times 6 = 18$ bits), so $X = 32 - (8 + 18) = 6$ bits. I-type has 2 register fields ($2 \times 6 = 12$ bits), so $Z = 32 - (8 + 12) = 12$ bits. Thus, $X + 2Y + Z = 6 + 2(8) + 12 = 34$.

Let $X$ be the bits for UNUSED, $Y$ for OPCODE, and $Z$ for immediate value/address. The value of $X + 2Y + Z$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐿1 be the language represented by the regular expression 𝑏∗𝑎𝑏∗(𝑎𝑏∗𝑎𝑏∗)∗
and 𝐿2 = {⁡𝑤∈(𝑎+ 𝑏)∗⁡|⁡⁡|𝑤| ≤4}, where |𝑤| denotes the length of string
𝑤. The number of strings in 𝐿2 which are also in 𝐿1 is ___________
questions.explaination: $L_1$ requires an odd number of $a$'s: strings containing either 1 or 3 $a$'s (since length $\le 4$). Length $\le 4$ with exactly one $a$: length 1 has $1$, length 2 has $2$, length 3 has $3$, length 4 has $4$ (total $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10$). Length $\le 4$ with exactly three $a$'s: length 3 has $aaa$ ($1$), length 4 has $\binom{4}{3} = 4$. Total strings in $L_1 \cap L_2 = 10 + 1 + 4 = 15$.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $L_1$ be the language represented by the regular expression $b^* a b^* (a b^* a b^*)^*$ and $L_2 = \{ w \in (a + b)^* \mid |w| \le 4 \}$, where $|w|$ denotes the length of string $w$. The number of strings in $L_2$ which are also in $L_1$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
Let 𝑍𝑛 be the group of integers {0, 1, 2, … , 𝑛−1} with addition modulo 𝑛 as the
group operation. The number of elements in the group 𝑍2 × 𝑍3 × 𝑍4 that are their
own inverses is ________

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru
questions.explaination: In an additive group, an element $x$ is its own inverse if $x + x \equiv 0 \pmod n \implies 2x \equiv 0 \pmod n$. In $\mathbb{Z}_2$, elements satisfying $2x \equiv 0$ are $\{0, 1\}$ (2 elements). In $\mathbb{Z}_3$, only $\{0\}$ satisfies $2x \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ (1 element). In $\mathbb{Z}_4$, $\{0, 2\}$ satisfy $2x \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (2 elements). In the direct product group $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_4$, total self-inverse elements $= 2 \times 1 \times 2 = 4$.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $Z_n$ be the group of integers $\{0, 1, 2, \dots, n-1\}$ with addition modulo $n$ as the group operation. The number of elements in the group $Z_2 \times Z_3 \times Z_4$ that are their own inverses is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
Consider a 32-bit system with 4 KB page size and page table entries of size 4 bytes
each. Assume 1 KB = 210 bytes. The OS uses a 2-level page table for memory
management, with the page table containing an outer page directory and an inner
page table. The OS allocates a page for the outer page directory upon process
creation. The OS uses demand paging when allocating memory for the inner page
table, i.e., a page of the inner page table is allocated only if it contains at least one
valid page table entry.
An active process in this system accesses 2000 unique pages during its execution,
and none of the pages are swapped out to disk. After it completes the page accesses,
let X denote the minimum and Y denote the maximum number of pages across the
two levels of the page table of the process.
The value of X+Y is ________
questions.explaination: Page size is $4\text{ KB} = 2^{12}$ bytes, PTE size is 4 bytes, so each page table holds $2^{12} / 4 = 1024$ entries. The process accesses 2000 unique pages. Minimum inner page tables $X$: $\lceil 2000 / 1024 \rceil = 2$ inner pages plus 1 outer page directory $= 3$. Maximum inner page tables $Y$: 2000 pages distributed across 2000 different inner tables, bounded by total possible entries in directory $= 1024$ inner pages plus 1 outer page directory $= 1025$. Hence, $X + Y = 3 + 1025 = 1028$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a 32-bit system with 4 KB page size and page table entries of size 4 bytes each. Assume $1\text{ KB} = 2^{10}$ bytes. The OS uses a 2-level page table for memory management, with an outer page directory and an inner page table. The OS allocates 1 page for the outer page directory upon process creation. The OS uses demand paging when allocating memory for the inner page table. An active process accesses 2000 unique pages during its execution. Let $X$ denote the minimum and $Y$ denote the maximum number of pages across the two levels of the page table of the process. The value of $X + Y$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

𝐴→𝑑#
𝐵→@
Let 𝐼0 = 𝐶𝐿𝑂𝑆𝑈𝑅𝐸({𝑆′ →⁡• 𝑆}). The number of items in the set 𝐺𝑂𝑇𝑂(𝐼0, 𝑆)
is ___________
questions.explaination: From $I_0 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S' \to \bullet S\})$, transitions on $S$ produce kernel items $\{S' \to S \bullet, S \to S \bullet S\}$.
